reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E4) directly shows nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, Mn at grain boundaries and links it to reduced cohesion and ductility loss, but the clustering was observed after deformation at 700°C, not after static thermal aging at 350–450°C. The hypothesis extrapolates the mechanism to a different, lower-temperature aging condition without direct evidence that such aging alone produces the same nanoclusters and embrittlement.
premises: Thermal aging at 350–450°C induces diffusion-driven nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, Mn at grain boundaries in single-phase CrMnFeCoNi.
These nanoclusters reduce grain boundary cohesion.
Reduced cohesion leads to intergranular cracking and brittle behavior under load.
This embrittlement occurs without secondary precipitate formation.
The mechanism is distinct from conventional impurity segregation or precipitate-driven embrittlement.
